summary: First iteration end-to-end testing of YLMS (Yazoo LIMS). Backend: 36 pytest tests covering health, auth, RBAC, products, tests catalog, reagents, equipment with calibration, full sample lifecycle (create -> executions start/submit/approve -> batch release -> CoA generation -> PDF download with QR), users, dashboard KPIs, audit log, and SPC reports - ALL PASSED. Frontend: login, dashboard with KPI cards and 14-day samples trend chart, and navigation across all 10 modules (samples, executions, batches, products, tests, reagents, equipment, users, audit, reports) verified. UI product creation + deletion happy path validated. No blocking bugs.

issues: Initial mount emits recharts warning 'width(-1) and height(-1)' before ResponsiveContainer measures. Cosmetic only; chart renders correctly. Consider adding minWidth/minHeight or aspect to ResponsiveContainer.

critical_code_review_comments: auth_utils.get_current_user uses request.cookies.get('access_token') fallback but /auth/login does NOT set an httpOnly cookie - only returns access_token JSON. Cookie fallback is dead code / inconsistent with playbook that expects httpOnly cookies. Either set the cookie on login (Set-Cookie httpOnly) or remove the cookie branch. Current flow works because the FE sends Bearer.

CORS_ORIGINS='*' with allow_credentials=True is a Starlette anti-pattern: browsers reject cookie-bearing responses when Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*'. If cookie-based auth is ever enabled, an explicit origin list is required.

samples router uses eval(formula, {'__builtins__':{}}, env) for the calc engine. Even with __builtins__ empty, expressions can access attribute chains (e.g. ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()). Since 'write' on executions is gated by RBAC, risk is limited to internal users, but this should be replaced by an AST/whitelist evaluator (e.g. asteval) before going to production.

log_audit inserts audit records but requests.list_audit uses require_permission('audit','read'). analyst / auxiliary have no audit permission - good. However, /api/audit lacks pagination beyond a 'limit' int, and no search-by-entity_id. Non-blocking.
dashboard turnaround loops through approved samples and re-parses ISO strings. Fine for small volume; consider Mongo aggregation for scale.

Batch release requires ALL executions to be approved/rejected but does NOT block release when meets_spec=False. If sample has any failed test, decision should default to 'blocked' with a warning. Currently the QM can still choose 'released' - business rule to confirm with domain.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all routes render + product CRUD via UI)

seed_data_creation: None persisted: pytest suite creates unique-code TEST- entities and cleans them up in a session teardown fixture. UI product test also self-cleans.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend covered by /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (run with `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -n 0`). NOTE: pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope, but this suite uses cross-class pytest attrs to chain product/test/sample IDs, so it MUST run serially with `-n 0`. Frontend UI happy path validated. If regressing, focus on the ExecutionDetail guided flow (reading-r1..r3 inputs, submit-execution, approve-execution) and Batches (release-batch-btn, decision-released, download-coa-*) which were validated at the API level but NOT clicked through in the UI in this iteration.
